AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Clinical education is a vital part of nursing students' learning; the importance of assessment tools and feedback in stimulating student learning has been stressed, but this needs to be studied in more detail.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To examine relationships between nursing students' perceptions of using an Assessment tool in Clinical Education (AssCE) during their mid-course discussion and final assessment, the content discussed during these meetings between the student, preceptor and nurse teacher and the students' overall perception of the clinical learning environment.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A cross-sectional, correlational design was used.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: A convenience sample of 110 nursing students from one Norwegian university college with two campuses.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Data were collected with self-developed questionnaires and analysed using logistic regression with SPSS and the PROCESS macro for mediation analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There was a positive relationship between nursing students' perceptions of using the assessment tool AssCE and their overall perception of the clinical learning environment. This relationship was, in turn, mediated by the content discussed during the formative mid-course discussion and summative final assessment.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Our conclusion is that the assessment tool AssCE supported students' clinical learning and that this relationship, in turn, was mediated by the degree to which the conversation during the assessment meeting focused on the student's knowledge, skills and professional judgement.
